newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dresdner sees further earnings improvement.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner sees further earnings improvement.

text.p: Dresdner Bank AG, Germany's second largest bank, on Tuesday said its first-half results provided a good basis for further earnings improvement in 1997.

The bank said in its interim report it expected to be able to pay an "appropriate" dividend for 1997 and also had scope to strengthen its equity capital base to an extent that would be at least commensurate to the dividend payout.
"Overall we are very pleased with the developments in the first half," Dresdner said. "But it would not be appropriate to extrapolate a full year result from this good result."
"However it represents a good base for a further -- and also qualitative -- improvement of our bank's earnings position," it said.
Dresdner reported a 23 percent rise in first-half operating profit after risk provisions to 1.743 billion marks in the first half of 1997, slightly above consensus forecast.

Dresdner said proceeds of almost 600 million marks from the sale of its stake in metals group Degussa AG would be booked in the second half of 1997. The profit will not flow into operating profits because it will be booked as income from financial investments.
Dresdner said it planned to place about half the profit in a tax-free reserve.
